newsitem.title: USA: Intel CEO sees major product transition.
newsitem.headline: Intel CEO sees major product transition.

text.p: Intel Corp chairman and chief executive Andrew Grove said Tuesday that the semiconductor maker is going through a "monumental" product transition this year.

Grove told reporters before adressing a New York analysts' meeting that its product transitions are so rapid that he estimates in the fourth quarter of this year about 90 percent of Intel's microprocessor revenues will come from new products, such as its Pentium processors with MMX technology and its new Pentium II processors.
He declined to comment further on the company's announcement on second-quarter earnings made last Friday.
On Friday, Intel said its second-quarter earnings would be below expectations, citing weaker than anticipated demand, especially in Europe.
"We told everything we know on business conditions Friday night," Grove said. "I can't really add to that. We won't add to that in the meeting."
Grove said that Europe is traditionally weaker in the second quarter and that this year it is weaker than usual.
"This year is a more marked decline," Grove said.
Grove said he did not want to speculate any further.
"My guess is that I am no better than any analyst at this point," he said, adding that Intel has about six more weeks before the end of the second quarter.

Grove said he remains "extremely bullish on this industry," adding that the advent of the Internet, interconnected PCs in networks and new applications in electronic commerce, health care and other areas will continue to fuel demand.
When asked about the current demand for personal computers, Grove said he does not see any change from current industry forecasts.
"I don't have any information on PC demand being any different (than current forecasts)," Grove said. "I don't have anything to add or subtract."
Some industry analysts have forecast personal computer growth worldwide at between about 17 percent and 19 percent this year.
